research_question: For historically low-SR categories (mug, basketball, laptop, bowl), after descriptive control for long-horizon task difficulty using expert_length, where do failures first appear in the observable chain: room arrival, nav-camera encounter, or post-visibility behavior?
hypothesis: H-EXPLORE: the dominant low-SR failure mass occurs before target visual encounter, through failure to reach the target room or put the target into the nav camera.
competing_explanation: H-DIFFICULTY or H-DOWNSTREAM: the low SR is largely explained by longer expert trajectories, or most failures occur after target visibility and therefore point downstream.
reference: Aligned historical full-200 run (200 tasks, 173 successes) plus narrow target-ID reanalysis. No new rollout.
repeat_or_treatment: Zero-rollout observational audit. Reproduce PI exploratory group/difficulty/stage counts from aligned raw evidence and build matched success controls; no treatment.
unique_variable: Primary comparison is predeclared low-SR category group versus reference categories within fixed expert_length strata. No physical-size variable is measured or tested.
fixed_conditions: Low-SR group fixed to mug.n.04, basketball.n.02, laptop.n.01, bowl.n.03
expert_length is a long-horizon proxy, not shortest path or pure environment difficulty
sub_house_id is sample index and cannot be used as difficulty
house_index may be reported as a scene stratum but not a numeric difficulty score
No GPU, simulator, SafeVLA execution, model load, episode or new size measurement
No neural Probe or intervention in this experiment
No causal claim from observational stage labels
metrics: expert_length mean/median by group and outcome
Optional success ~ low_sr_group + log1p(expert_length) sensitivity model
S0/S1/S2a/S2b counts and proportions for low-SR and reference failures
Same-category and cross-category nearest-control expert_length gaps
expected_result: Either formalize that pre-visibility exploration/room-arrival dominates low-SR failures and remains after coarse difficulty stratification, or redirect the next mechanism experiment toward downstream visual/readout/termination or general long-horizon difficulty.
falsifying_result: H-EXPLORE is weakened if most low-SR failures are post-visibility S2 or if the low-SR performance gap largely disappears within expert_length strata.
alternative_explanations: expert_length captures only part of task difficulty and is not shortest-path distance
house/scene geometry and initial target distance may confound the comparison
room visitation and visible pixels are policy outcomes, not exogenous task difficulty
small sample counts within categories can make stage proportions unstable
the user's qualitative small-object grouping is not itself a causal size measurement
stop_conditions: Aligned historical raw evidence cannot be reconciled
expert_length cannot be tied to the same task identities
required room/visibility fields are missing for failures
new model/simulator/episode execution would be required
any Probe/intervention or physical-size analysis would start automatically
